verdict.root_cause: Checkout's errors are a downstream symptom. In every failing trace the error sits on a checkout-side outbound HTTP POST client span ending in EOF with no server-side child span, meaning the callee closed the connection mid-request and produced no span of its own [tr_13b302399095]. Email matches that description: it serves plain HTTP POSTs on port 6060 and emits no span-call metrics under its service name in either window, so it would be invisible in trace topology [tr_d25404675376][tr_71ba4f61b489]. Email's log shows healthy 200s early in the window, then nothing but three complete Sinatra/Puma boot sequences at ~02:35:54, 02:36:16 and 02:36:44 — a ~25s crash-restart cycle where the process boots fully, binds its listener, reaches serving state, then dies with no exception or error text at all [tr_71ba4f61b489]. A process that starts cleanly, serves briefly, and is killed silently on a short repeating cycle is terminated from outside the application — the signature of a kill for exceeding a resource limit. Each kill severs in-flight connections, producing checkout's EOFs and the partial, bursty error ratio (mean ~1.2%, peak ~7.4%, change point 02:32:46) rather than a total outage [tr_f643c74d6f9c]. No change landed near onset on either service: checkout's CURRENCY_ADDR flapping ended ~19.8h earlier on the revert side and email's image flapping ~16.4h earlier, also net-reverted [tr_54f09d5ac3cd][tr_85aed0c53f6b].
verdict.reasoning: The failing hop is a childless EOF on a checkout HTTP client span — a connection closed by the callee, not a timeout or a downstream error status; cart, currency, payment, product-catalog and shipping were all explicitly cleared in the same traces [tr_13b302399095]. Email is the plausible callee that leaves no server span because it emits no span metrics at all, in baseline as well as incident [tr_d25404675376]. Email is simultaneously in a boot-serve-die loop with no error output [tr_71ba4f61b489]; the silence at death discriminates the mechanism, since bad config, an unreachable dependency, a corrupt store or a full disk all write something, and a bad artifact fails during init rather than after binding the port — both ruled out there. The partial, bursty error shape fits each fresh instance serving most requests and failing only those in flight at kill time [tr_f643c74d6f9c]. Checkout itself keeps producing spans and tolerates the failure, continuing to EmptyCart, ship and publish, so it is the noticer, not the culprit [tr_13b302399095].
open_questions: No memory, CPU, fd or OOM-kill evidence for email was gathered; the exhaustion mechanism is inferred from the silent-kill signature. Container exit codes, restart counts and a memory series would settle it.
The erroring callee is inferred, not proven — the POST span names no target; confirming checkout's outbound host/port for the confirmation call would close it.
Email's log was truncated (oldest 8, newest 32 lines), so 02:05-02:35 is unobserved and the exact first-crash time is unknown.

alternatives.root_cause: Email is crash-looping on a bad image or artifact left behind by the automated image flapping, killing connections checkout holds open.
alternatives.why_not: Every boot sequence runs to completion and binds the port before the process dies, which is not how a broken artifact fails; the image flapping also net-reverted ~16.4h before onset [tr_85aed0c53f6b][tr_71ba4f61b489].

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout itself is the fault — an in-process stall or broken outbound client produces the EOF and the unexplained self-time, independent of any callee.
alternatives.why_not: It does not explain email's concurrent restart loop, and an EOF status is a peer-closed connection rather than a local stall; checkout otherwise completes its work normally [tr_13b302399095][tr_71ba4f61b489].

proposal.expected_effect: No action taken. Email will keep emitting Sinatra/Puma boot banners every ~22-28s in {service="email"}, and checkout's span error ratio will keep bursting around a ~1.2% mean. Abstaining because the named fix class (scale) is unavailable here, and no permitted action fits: rollback_image and revert_config require a change inside the window, but email's only changes are matched image update/revert pairs ending ~16.4h before onset, net-reverted [tr_85aed0c53f6b]. restart_service nominally matches process state, but the world is already recreating this process every ~25s [tr_71ba4f61b489], so a recreate predicts no observable change. Next step is evidence: email's container exit code, restart count and memory series, plus the outbound host:port on checkout's erroring POST span.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if email stops cycling and resumes 200-status access lines with no action, and checkout's error ratio returns to zero — the fault was transient. Also falsified if a restart makes email serve cleanly well past ~25s. Note the callee is inferred: the erroring POST names no target and has no server-side child [tr_13b302399095], so no observable today directly confirms email.
proposal.risk: Abstaining lets checkout keep losing ~1.2% of spans (peaks ~7.4%) and keeps order-confirmation emails undelivered while diagnosis continues. If the kill is in fact something a clean recreate would clear, that delay is my error.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change; the current degradation persists for checkout and its callers frontend and frontend-proxy, and for email's inbound traffic.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity with two independent seeds (checkout and email) alerting a minute apart and a wide downstream radius — not dismissible, and no open incident to attach it to.
